subject: On-prem module compatibility sweep + GitLab pipeline ops
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Pete Larson <plarson@acmecloud.com>, rack-support@rackvendor.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: On-prem module compatibility sweep + GitLab pipeline ops

Team / Pete,

We have a request from AcmeCloud to certify the Terraform/Helm/Ansible modules we intend to ship with the next private deployment bundle for their on-prem racks. Goals for this thread:

- Surface any breaking API/variable changes between current modules and the 1.6.x onprem image.
- Identify minimal GitLab CI changes needed to run the preflight matrix (terraform fmt/validate/plan for each module, helm lint + template, ansible-lint + syntax-check).
- Flag security-sensitive network defaults (open CIDRs, hostNetwork: true, privileged DaemonSets) for remediation before delivery.

Attachments: module-compatibility-matrix.xlsx (working sheet with modules + tested versions) and gitlab-pipeline-snippets.md (initial CI templates). Pete — if you can attach the rack-level network diagram that shows patch panel and uplink VLANs, that will help us map service CIDRs to the physical segments.

Quick asks:
1) Internal owners — can each of you review the matrix for your modules and add an Owner + Risk column by EOD Thursday (5/14)?
2) Marcus — can you run the GitLab pipeline snippets in a sandbox runner and paste any failure logs to the Drive link?
3) Pete / Rack support — can you confirm whether the on-prem load balancer will SNAT (source NAT) or preserve client IPs? This affects our service annotations and egress policies.

I'll consolidate and propose a remediation plan (if anything is flagged) and a schedule for the preflight runs.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Manager, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: module-compatibility-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
[Attachment: gitlab-pipeline-snippets.md (text/markdown)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Pete Larson <plarson@acmecloud.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem module compatibility sweep + GitLab pipeline ops

Hannah — quick notes after a first pass on the matrix:

- terraform/privnet-module: variable rename (v1.4 -> v1.5) changed "internal_network" -> "service_cidr". I've left a note in column 'Owner' and added a suggested compatibility wrapper in TF (locals + deprecated variable warning).
- helm/web-proxy: default "hostNetwork: true" was enabled in the chart values file only for our lab profile; production onprem bundle should explicitly set hostNetwork: false and use hostPort where strictly necessary.
- ansible/node-config: module requires python3.10 on target hosts; we need to document this preflight package check.

I ran the CI snippet for terraform validate on the privnet module in a sandbox runner; two modules failed because of a provider source pin (hashicorp/aws) mismatch — stack trace and the failing job log are in the Drive link.

I'll add suggested fixes in the matrix and raise PRs for the TF wrappers this week. Marcus — if the runner environment differs (docker executor vs shell), some of the linter behavior will change — please note which executor you used.

- Aditya
Aditya Rao
Staff SRE, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Pete Larson <plarson@acmecloud.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: rack-support@rackvendor.com, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:53:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: On-prem module compatibility sweep + GitLab pipeline ops

Hannah — attaching the rack-level network diagram and short answers below.

- Diagram attached: rack-network-diagram.pdf (shows management VLANs, two uplinks per rack, and the LB placement).
- The on-prem load balancer by default preserves client IPs for TCP flows (no SNAT), but our deployment automation sits behind an F5 that can be configured to SNAT if required.
- Uplink VLANs: 110 (mgmt), 220 (services), 330 (storage). Please note our firewall policy blocks all upstream outbound except 443/123/53 from the services VLAN.

If you need a maintenance window for running preflight scripts against staging racks, we can open a 2-hour slot on Thursday morning (UTC).

Thanks,
Pete Larson
Solutions Architect
AcmeCloud
[Attachment: rack-network-diagram.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Pete Larson <plarson@acmecloud.com>, rack-support@rackvendor.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 13:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem module compatibility sweep + GitLab pipeline ops

Team — summary and decisions after reviewing the matrix + logs: 

1) Owners: Aditya (privnet + security hooks), Marcus (CI runner + helm tests), Irene (ansible/node-config). Please update the matrix Owner and Risk columns by Thursday EOD.
2) Immediate fixes (short-lived PRs this week):
   - terraform: add variable aliasing and provider pin reconciliation (Aditya).
   - helm: set hostNetwork:false in onprem values and add explicit service annotations for preserved client IP (Marcus).
   - ansible: add a preflight role that checks python version and required packages (Irene).
3) CI changes: Marcus to spawn a GitLab ephemeral runner with docker+privileged=false; run terraform fmt/validate/plan, helm lint/template, ansible-lint. Capture artifacts and push to the Drive folder.
4) Network constraints acknowledged: AcmeCloud will allow a Thursday morning maintenance slot (UTC) to run preflight. Pete — please confirm the exact UTC window (we'll post it to the matrix).
5) Compliance note: any change that relaxes firewall rules or requires SNAT must go through security review. We will flag those in the matrix and stop the delivery if required.

I'll own the remediation tracker and proposed delivery cadence — planning to publish a short checklist by Friday with PR links and CI run IDs.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
